name: Should I add an island, peninsula, or skip both in my small kitchen?

mainEntity.name: Should I add an island, peninsula, or skip both in my small kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: An island is not automatically an improvement; it must leave enough usable circulation and preserve preparation space. A peninsula, shorter island, single-wall arrangement, or improved perimeter storage may work better in a compact kitchen. Compare seating capacity, cabinet storage, countertop area, appliance access, and the effect on nearby dining or living spaces. Mark the proposed footprint on the floor with tape and test walking routes and open doors. Elite Remodeling & Design can develop alternatives based on the existing room and intended use.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose an island only if it preserves comfortable movement, appliance access, preparation space, and needed seating. A peninsula or better perimeter storage may provide more function in a compact room. Tape the proposed footprint on the floor before deciding.
